# 1 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_003_page_001.jpg

---

1. His son Judas, called Maccabeus, stepped into his father's place.
2. All his brothers backed him, and everyone who had joined his father. With gladness they fought the battles of Israel.
3. He spread glory wide across his people. He strapped on armor like a giant, buckled on his weapons, set his battle lines, and covered his troops with his sword.
4. His deeds were like a lion's, like a young lion screaming for its kill.
5. He hunted the lawbreakers down and stalked them; he burned those who terrorized his people.
6. The lawless fell back in fear of him. Every evildoer panicked. Victory was worked out in his hands.
7. He made kings bitter and Jacob glad; his memory is blessed for all time.
8. He went through the cities of Judah, rooted out the ungodly, and turned away wrath from Israel.
9. His name spread to the ends of the earth. He gathered back the scattered.
10. Apollonius mustered the Gentiles — drawing on Samaria's manpower — and assembled a large, powerful force to make war on Israel.
11. Judas got word and marched out to meet him. He struck Apollonius down, killed him, and left the field littered with the dead. The survivors ran.
12. His men stripped the battlefield. Judas took Apollonius's own sword, and he fought with it for the rest of his life.
13. When Seron, commander of the Syrian army, heard that Judas had gathered a fighting force — faithful men who stood with him —
14. he said: "I'll make my name here. I'll earn glory in the kingdom. I'll crush Judas and his followers, the ones who spit on the king's command."
15. A strong force of lawless men came with him to do it, to take revenge on Israel.
16. He pushed forward to the pass at Beth-horon. Judas came out to meet him with only a small band of men.
17. When Judas's men looked up and saw the army bearing down on them, they said: "How are we supposed to fight this? There are only a handful of us. We haven't even eaten today — we're barely standing."
18. Judas answered: "It's easy for many to be trapped by few. It makes no difference to Heaven — many or few, salvation is salvation.
19. Victory in battle doesn't come from having the bigger army. Strength comes down from Heaven.
20. They march against us soaked in arrogance and lawlessness. Their goal is to wipe us out — us, our wives, our children — and loot what's left.
21. We fight for our lives and our laws.
22. God himself will shatter them in front of us. Don't be afraid of them."
23. He stopped talking and charged. Suddenly. Seron and his whole army collapsed before him.
24. Judas drove them down the Beth-horon descent all the way to the plain. Eight hundred of them lay dead. The rest bolted for Philistine territory.
25. After that, the fear of Judas and his brothers gripped every nation around them. Word reached the king. Everyone was talking about the battles Judas was fighting.
26. When King Antiochus heard the reports, he erupted in fury. He sent out orders and called up every military force in his kingdom — a truly massive army.
27. He cracked open his treasury and gave the troops a full year's pay, ordering them ready for anything.
28. Then he saw the problem: the treasury was draining fast and the province revenues were thin — a consequence of the conflict and disorder he himself had created by tearing up the customs that had been in place since ancient times.
29. He was afraid he wouldn't have the resources he needed — for his usual lavish spending, his gifts, his habit of outspending every king before him.
30. He was deeply troubled and decided to march to Persia, squeeze the tribute out of those provinces, and come back flush with money.
31. He left Lysias — a man of standing, royal blood — to manage all royal affairs from the Euphrates to the Egyptian border,
32. and to raise the young prince Antiochus until his return.
33. He handed Lysias half the army and the war elephants. He gave him detailed instructions — what he wanted done, especially concerning the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
34. Lysias was to send a force against them, crush them, and uproot Israel's strength and the remnant of Jerusalem. He was to erase their memory from that place.
35. He was to settle foreigners throughout the entire territory and distribute the land by lot.
36. The king took the other half of the forces and marched out from Antioch, his capital city, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year. He crossed the Euphrates and pushed into the eastern provinces.
37. Lysias chose three of the king's powerful inner circle — Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias —
38. and dispatched them with forty thousand infantry and seven thousand cavalry to march into Judah and lay it waste, as the king had ordered.
39. They set out with their full force and pitched camp near Emmaus in the coastal plain.
40. Word spread to the merchants of the region. They came to the camp carrying enormous quantities of silver and gold and chains, expecting to buy up Israeli slaves. Auxiliary forces from Syria and the surrounding territories joined them.
41. Judas and his brothers took stock: the crisis was deepening, enemy forces were inside their territory, and they knew the king's orders — total destruction, complete annihilation of the people.
42. They said to one another: "We have to rebuild what has been ruined. We fight for our people and for the sanctuary."
43. The congregation gathered to prepare for battle and to pray, asking God for mercy and compassion.
44. Jerusalem sat empty as a desert. Not one of her children came in or went out. The sanctuary was under foreign boots. The citadel had become a barracks for the nations. Joy had left Jacob. The music had stopped.
45. They gathered and traveled to Mizpah, facing Jerusalem — the old prayer-site of Israel.
46. They fasted, dressed in sackcloth, poured ashes on their heads, and tore their clothes.
47. They unrolled the Torah scrolls — the very scrolls the Gentiles had smeared with idol-paint.
48. They presented the priestly vestments, the firstfruits, the tithes. They brought forward the Nazirites who had completed their vow period.
49. They cried to Heaven: "What should we do with these men? Where do we take them?
50. Your sanctuary is trampled, defiled. Your priests are in mourning and disgrace.
51. Now the Gentiles are closing in to destroy us. You know what they have planned for us.
52. How can we stand against them without your help?"
53. They blew the trumpets. The shouting rose up.
54. Then Judas organized the army. He appointed commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
55. Anyone who had a house under construction, anyone who had just become engaged, anyone who had just planted a vineyard, anyone who was afraid — he told them to go home. The Torah said so.
56. The army moved and camped to the south of Emmaus.
57. Judas addressed them: "Strap on your weapons. Be soldiers. At dawn we fight these Gentiles who are massed against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
58. Better to die in battle than to stand by and watch our nation and our holy place be destroyed.
59. Whatever Heaven wills — that is what will happen."
60. Gorgias took five thousand infantry and a thousand elite cavalry and led the force out by night
